record.paper_title: Combinatorial properties of continuous graphs: A survey of challenges, solutions and open problems
record.original_question: Let β_r(Γ) denote the minimum cardinality of an r-cover of a continuous graph Γ, where an r-cover is a family of radius-r balls whose union contains every point of Γ. In the computationally hard cases where r is a non-unit rational fraction, what lower bounds can be proved for the approximation hardness of the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs?

evidence.quote: Definition 10. Given a positive real number r, a set of balls B = {B(p, r) : p ∈ E} is called an r-cover of Γ if for any point q ∈ E there is a ball B ∈ B containing q. The r-cover number of Γ is the cardinality of the minimum r-cover in Γ further denoted as βr(Γ) or βr for simplicity.

We suggest the following straightforward open question: For the hard cases of the problem (with the radius being a non-unit fraction, see Hartmann et al [16]), what are the lower bounds for the inapproximability of the minimum r-cover problem?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a continuous graph, that is, a metric space obtained from a finite simple graph by viewing each edge as a unit-length interval isometric to $[0,1]$, and let $E$ also denote the underlying point set of this metric space (the union of all edges and vertices). For a point $p \in E$ and a real number $r>0$, let $B(p,r)=\{q\in E : d_\Gamma(p,q)\le r\}$ denote the closed metric ball of radius $r$ centered at $p$. A family $\mathcal{B}=\{B(p_i,r) : i=1,\dots,k\}$ is called an $r$-cover of $\Gamma$ if every point $q\in E$ belongs to at least one $B(p_i,r)$. Define the $r$-cover number $\beta_r(\Gamma)$ to be the minimum cardinality of an $r$-cover of $\Gamma$.

It is known that computing $\beta_r(\Gamma)$ is computationally hard when $r$ is a positive rational number that is not a unit fraction (i.e., $r\notin\{1/n : n\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\}$). For such fixed values of $r$, determine non-trivial lower bounds on the approximation ratio achievable in polynomial time for the minimum $r$-cover problem on continuous graphs. In particular, prove an explicit constant (or super-constant) inapproximability factor for $\beta_r$, under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions such as $\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}$ or the Unique Games Conjecture.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a straightforward open question regarding inapproximability lower bounds for the minimum r-cover problem on continuous graphs in the hard regime (non-unit-fraction r). Related work by Hartmann et al. and recent results on approximating δ-covering establish hardness and provide approximation algorithms with conditional lower bounds, but no specific inapproximability bound for the continuous r-cover problem in the non-unit-fraction case appears to have been established. The status remains open.

status_evidence.title: Approximating δ-Covering
status_evidence.snippet: Hartmann et al. studied a continuous facility location/covering problem on graphs; FPT for δ ≤ 2 and W[1]-hard otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Related hardness results exist but a specific inapproximability lower bound for non-unit-fraction r in the continuous r-cover problem is not established.
